newsitem.title: UK: UK natgas dull and quiet, main players out of market.
newsitem.headline: UK natgas dull and quiet, main players out of market.

text.p: The UK spot natural gas market was barely traded beyond the first day forward on Wednesday, with many traders attending a meeting on the flexibility mechanism called by Transco.
On the within day and day ahead markets, prices softened following the recent system buys on the flexibility mechanism on Monday and Tuesday.
These had pushed up the within day price on Tuesday to 14.30 pence a therm or above, but the levels fell significantly on Wednesday.
Within day gas was traded at 11.00 pence at St Fergus and at up to 11.50 pence at Bacton, but dealers said the higher levels of Tuesday were now gone.
The day-ahead market was slightly busier, with one player buying 500,000 therms of gas and with over 800,000 therms confirmed done.
The price was also slightly weaker, but the movement was not considered significant by traders or brokers in such a thin market.
Further forward, trade was almost non-existent. Just one deal for the third quarter was seen at 10.60 pence a therm, and a brokers summed up the activity by calling it "a waste of a day."
The IPE futures market was equally dismal, with only two deals covering 50 lots done in February.

It was reported that these represented a mistake in any case - a dealer had apparently done the first trade, at 17.50 pence a therm, in error and then backed out of the position with the same counterparty at a lower price shortly afterwards. This was not confirmed.
Gas demand was forecast to fall slightly on Thursday as the unseasonally cold weather improves slightly.
Transco puts demand at 237 mcm or 55 percent of peak demand, down from 248 mcm/58 percent on Wednesday.
The temperature is forecast to rise from 6.1 Celsius to 7.5 Celsius, still well below the seasonal normal 12.1 Celsius.
